title: IRA Drug Price Negotiation — Cycle 3 Live
catalyst: Cycle 1 prices (10 drugs, 38–79% discounts) took effect Jan 2026. Cycle 3 underway — first-ever Part B drug negotiations and renegotiations; prices effective 2028. CMS-4215-P codification comment period closed Aug 17, 2026.
implications: AbbVie, Merck, Amgen face multi-billion annual Medicare revenue reductions
MA/Part D formulary redesign cascades to PBMs (Capital Rx) and MA plans (SCAN, Oscar, Alignment)
Patient access programs (ConnectiveRx, EVERSANA) restructure as out-of-pocket caps shift manufacturer concession math
Regulatory science firms (Certara) see rising demand as pharma builds evidence for price justification
Companion diagnostics (Guardant) tied to negotiated drugs face formulary and access ripple effects

title: CMS-0057-F Prior Auth APIs — Jan 2027 Deadline
catalyst: January 2027 compliance deadline for four mandated FHIR APIs covering MA, Medicaid MCOs, and ACA marketplace plans. Prior auth decision timeframes compressed to 72 hours (expedited) and 7 days (standard).
implications: SCAN, Alignment, Oscar, Partnership HealthPlan, SFHP all face mandated API buildout — IT spend rising
Epic's implementation roadmap becomes a critical dependency for health system compliance
Redox and Smile Digital Health positioned as essential middleware; Notable benefits from PA workflow automation volume
Prior auth denial rates likely to fall as transparency increases — downstream revenue risk for utilization management businesses
CHAI AI governance frameworks become more urgent as payers deploy AI for automated prior auth decisions

title: MA Risk Adjustment Tightening (HCC V28 + RADV)
catalyst: HCC V28 model transition reduces average MA risk scores — compressing plan revenue. RADV extrapolation methodology finalized. DOJ scrutiny of retrospective chart chase and upcoding intensifying across major MA plans.
implications: SCAN, Alignment, Oscar face revenue headwinds — per-member-per-month margins under pressure
Coding accuracy programs intensify; risk adjustment vendors (Acumen, RTI) see demand rise
Alignment's owned-provider model provides some insulation; pure plan models (Oscar) more exposed
MA enrollment growth may slow as plans exit unprofitable markets or raise premiums
RTI and CMS contractors evaluating whether V28 achieves intended overbilling correction without overcorrection

title: TEAM Model — Mandatory Episode Accountability
catalyst: CMS mandatory bundled payment model for surgical episodes (joint replacement, CABG, spinal fusion) launches in selected regions. No opt-out. First mandatory CMMI model since CJR. Episodes cover 90-day post-acute period.
implications: AdventHealth and other large health systems in selected markets face direct episode risk
Post-acute referral network optimization becomes a financial imperative — SNF and HH quality differentiation is now contractual
August Health (SNF care management) sees premium on PAC coordination capability
Hinge Health surgical decision support adjacent to TEAM joint replacement episodes
Care navigation for ACO REACH beneficiaries overlapping TEAM episodes creates attribution complexity

title: MIPS Sunset Proposal — Advanced APM Pressure (2029)
catalyst: CY2027 PFS proposed rule signals sunsetting of traditional MIPS beginning the 2029 performance year. Clinicians face binary choice: qualify into an Advanced APM track or face growing payment adjustments under a restructured program.
implications: Privia Health and Astrana face accelerated physician migration pressure into ACO REACH and other Advanced APM tracks
Independent practices without VBC infrastructure face meaningful payment pressure — consolidation accelerator
RTI's QPP evaluation contract scope likely expands as CMS builds transition evidence base
Oscar and Alignment must redesign value-based physician contracting to align with Advanced APM qualification
Coalition for Health AI (CHAI) AI quality measure governance becomes more critical as AI-generated quality data enters APM scoring

title: AI Governance Fragmentation — Three Regimes, No Reconciliation
catalyst: FDA finalized PCCP guidance (Aug 2025) for continuously-learning AI devices, ONC's HTI-1 transparency rule took effect Jan 2025, and CHAI's model-card registry (3,000+ members) partnered with the Joint Commission (Sept 2025) on a certification track for 22,000+ accredited hospitals — three parallel regimes, mandatory and voluntary, with no single authority reconciling them.
implications: Health systems (Kaiser, Providence, Cleveland Clinic) face three overlapping AI governance obligations rather than one
ModelOp and other CHAI-certified assurance providers compete to operationalize recurring model validation as the de facto trust layer
Liability for algorithm-driven coverage denials (MA prior-auth) remains unresolved even as FDA/ONC/CHAI regimes mature
State-level AI laws (Utah, Colorado, Texas) add a fourth layer of fragmentation on top of the federal regimes
Notable and other AI-enabled clinical automation vendors must track FDA device rules, ONC transparency rules, and CHAI/Joint Commission certification simultaneously
